summary: Sudden spike in 5xx errors: API gateway 502/503 and upstream runtime crashes during traffic burst for Dedicated customer
description:
Issue summary:
During a customer traffic spike on 2026-03-10 ~09:10-11:40 UTC, Nimbus Analytics observed a sharp rise in 5xx responses (502/503 and occasional 500) from the Redwood API endpoint. The API gateway returned transient 502/503 errors, and downstream serving runtime logs show repeated process crashes (OOM and assertion failures) on several GPU workers.

Impact:
- Multiple production routes for Nimbus subject to increased error rates (~12% 5xx for a 20 minute window, baseline <0.2%).
- Customer reported failed batch jobs and decreased SLA compliance.
- A subset of other dedicated customers on the same tenant pool reported elevated latencies but not full failure.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant: nimbus-prod-01
- Region: us-west primary, some traffic routed to us-east failover
- Models: redwood-v2-large (primary), vicuna-13b (fallback)
- Serving runtime version: runtime@v2.8.1 (deployed 2026-03-01)
- Autoscaler version: autoscaler@1.3.0

Steps to reproduce (customer traffic pattern):
1. Customer sent sustained high-concurrency inference workload: 600 concurrent connections, average sequence length 1024 tokens, many streaming responses with long-tail KV cache usage.
2. Errors begin within ~3-5 minutes of sustained concurrency and ramp to peak within 15 minutes.
3. Errors reduce after traffic drops or when we applied throttling and restarted a subset of runtime workers.

Logs / Observations (excerpts):
- api-gateway: "upstream temporarily unavailable (503)" and "502 bad gateway: connection reset by peer"
- serving-runtime: repeated "terminate due to OOM" followed by "assertion failed: kv_cache_index < capacity" in runtime logs
- kernel OOM messages on hosts: "Out of memory: Killed process 11234 (runtime_worker)"
- autoscaler: observed delayed scaling; pool utilization shows many nodes saturated while new nodes took longer than expected to register.

Initial hypothesis:
- High concurrent streaming requests with long sequence lengths cause memory pressure on runtime leading to OOMs and crashes.
- Autoscaler latency in provisioning new GPU workers contributed to overload; some workers were experiencing noisy-neighbor memory spikes.
- API gateway returned 502/503 when upstream connections were closed unexpectedly by crashed runtime processes.

Urgency and business impact:
- Customer-facing production impact for an enterprise customer on dedicated cluster; SLA risk. Prioritized as P1/Sev1.

Workaround applied so far:
- Applied temporary global throttle to Nimbus tenant (reduced concurrency cap to 200 connections) which reduced error rate to <1% within 10 minutes.
- Restarted 6 affected runtime worker pods (rolled sequentially) to clear OOM state and reclaimed memory.
- Increased autoscaler target min capacity for the tenant pool as a short-term protection.

Next steps / Action items:
- Engineering (SRE + Runtime) to reproduce load in staging with equivalent concurrency and sequence lengths. (Assigned: Marcus Patel).
- Add heap/KV cache telemetry to runtime crash reports to get exact memory utilization at time of crash. (Assigned: Runtime team).
- Short-term: adjust autoscaler warm-pool sizing and reduce provisioning latency (PR open).
- Medium-term: improve KV cache eviction policy and guardrails for long streaming sessions.
- Postmortem to be created under INC-2026-03-10-01 once full root cause confirmed.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:35 - Support (Avery): Received alert from Nimbus CS that they are seeing 502/503s. Opened ticket and began initial triage. Notified SRE.

2026-03-10 09:48 - SRE (Marcus): Observed OOM kills on nimbus-prod-01 workers. Temporarily throttled tenant to reduce errors. Restarted affected pods; errors reduced. Will investigate autoscaler behaviour.

2026-03-10 10:20 - Customer (Nimbus - Elena Rao): Throttle reduced errors but we lost ~15 minutes of data during batch window. Need estimate for full remediation and whether additional retries will be safe.

2026-03-10 12:05 - Runtime lead (Sana Iqbal): Reproduced similar OOM locally with synthetic traffic hitting KV cache; hypothesis that cache growth combined with long sequences triggers unbounded memory growth. Working on safe cap and eviction policy.

2026-03-11 15:00 - Autoscaler engineer (Diego Morales): Found race in node registration that delayed worker registration under high churn; PR #214 opened to increase registration retries and reduce cold-start latency.
2026-03-12 08:30 - Support (Avery): Notified customer of temporary mitigations and ETA for next update. Postmortem draft requested after root cause verified.
2026-03-14 11:00 - Marcus: Assigned long-term tasks to runtime team and scheduling a canary with kv-cap applied to a small percentage of tenant pool next week.
investigation_notes: Key leads: reproduce in staging with 600 concurrent streams and long sequences. Instrument KV cache allocations and add guardrails. Autoscaler changes merged to reduce registration latency; monitor for reduced errors after canary. Consider eviction by prefix frequency or age. Check for any recent changes to runtime memory accounting (no new releases since 2026-03-01).
resolution: Triage complete. Short-term: throttled tenant and restarted workers reduced error rate to acceptable levels; autoscaler patch merged (PR #214) to reduce registration latency; runtime patch to cap KV cache allocations and add eviction policy in progress (runtime PR #881). Long-term: schedule canary deployment and postmortem once canary validated. Customer notified and monitoring dashboards updated.
